quests.instruction: On the open highway, the school bus speeds up. Near the school gate, where a ‘Children Crossing’ sign stands, the driver…
quests.hint: What does a careful driver do when kids might step into the road?
quests.explanation: Speeding up makes you go faster. Slowing down makes you go slower, which is the safe choice near children.
quests.funFact: Speed limits are often lower near schools because children can step out suddenly.

quests.instruction: Pavan is late for the bus, so he has to hurry. Once he reaches the stop, there’s nothing to do but…
quests.hint: At a bus stop, people stay put until the bus comes into view.
quests.explanation: To hurry is to move quickly because time is short. To wait is to stay put until something happens.
quests.funFact: The word “queue” comes from the French word for “tail”.

quests.instruction: Anil caught a small fish and held it up for a photo. Then he gently ___ it back into the lake.
quests.hint: What should you do for a fish you don’t plan to eat?
quests.explanation: Holding keeps something in your grip. Releasing lets it go.
quests.funFact: Many fishing spots have catch-and-release rules to protect the fish.

quests.instruction: Mama and I dug a small hole for the mango sapling. After setting its roots inside, we…
quests.hint: What happens to a hole once the plant is in place?
quests.explanation: Digging takes soil out to make a hole. Filling in puts soil back to cover it up.
quests.funFact: Plant roots need air as well as soil, so the earth shouldn’t be packed down too hard.

quests.instruction: Dad lights the candle on the birthday cake. After the song, Chloe takes a big breath to…
quests.hint: A big breath, a wish, and then the flame is gone.
quests.explanation: To light a flame is to start it burning. To put it out is to stop it.
quests.funFact: A flame needs oxygen, which is why a candle goes out under an upside-down jar.

quests.instruction: The plane sped down the runway, lifted into the air and took off. Two hours later, it was time to…
quests.hint: What does the pilot do when the airport appears below?
quests.explanation: Taking off is leaving the ground. Landing is coming back down onto it.
quests.funFact: Planes usually take off and land facing into the wind, because it helps them lift and slow down.

quests.instruction: Kalu the cat chases a toy mouse across the floor. A real mouse in the same situation would be trying to…
quests.hint: Which way would a frightened mouse run?
quests.explanation: Chasing means running after something. Escaping means getting away from whatever is after you.
quests.funFact: House mice can squeeze through gaps about as narrow as a pencil.

quests.instruction: Meena was explaining her drawing when her brother talked over her. After he stopped, she was happy to…
quests.hint: Once the interruption is over, the storyteller picks up where he left off.
quests.explanation: Interrupting breaks into what someone is doing or saying. Continuing carries on from where they were.
quests.funFact: In many cultures, waiting until someone finishes speaking is seen as polite.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “hello”? (waving to a friend as they arrive vs. waving as they leave)
quests.hint: Which word do you call out as the car pulls away?
quests.explanation: Hello is how we greet someone. Goodbye is how we part from them.
quests.funFact: “Goodbye” began as a short form of “God be with you”.

quests.instruction: Rhea loves drawing, so she joined the art club. If she stopped going and told the teacher she wasn’t coming back, she would…
quests.hint: What does someone do when they leave a team for good?
quests.explanation: To join is to become part of a group. To quit is to leave it.
quests.funFact: The Scouts movement, begun in 1907, is one of the biggest youth groups in the world.

quests.instruction: Bilal’s sleeves were too long, so Mum shortened them. When he grows taller next year, she may need to…
quests.hint: Think of what a tailor does when a child grows.
quests.explanation: Shortening makes something less long. Lengthening makes it longer.
quests.funFact: Many children’s clothes have a hem that can be let down as kids grow.

quests.instruction: Before bed, the children tidy up their toys. Minutes later, the crawling baby can easily…
quests.hint: What does a baby do with a neat pile of blocks?
quests.explanation: Tidying puts things in order. Messing up scatters them again.
quests.funFact: In many Japanese schools, students clean their own classrooms every day.

quests.instruction: Grandfather teaches Aisha how to play chess. While he is the teacher, Aisha is…
quests.hint: Who is gaining a new skill in this picture?
quests.explanation: Teaching is passing knowledge on. Learning is receiving it.
quests.funFact: Chess was invented in India about fifteen hundred years ago.

quests.instruction: In class discussion, Mr. Das says: speak clearly when it’s your turn, and when someone else is talking, you…
quests.hint: While your mouth is closed, your ears do the work.
quests.explanation: Speaking sends your words out. Listening takes someone else’s words in.
quests.funFact: You can tell which direction a sound comes from because you have one ear on each side of your head.

quests.instruction: Zubin pressed play on the cartoon. When his mum called him to lunch, he pressed…
quests.hint: Which button freezes the picture so you can come back later?
quests.explanation: Play makes the video run. Pause stops it where it is without losing your place.
quests.funFact: Most apps use ▶ for “play” and ⏸ for “pause”.

quests.instruction: To see the ladybug’s tiny spots, Tara zoomed in on her tablet. To see the whole garden again, she zoomed…
quests.hint: Which way do you move your fingers to make the picture smaller?
quests.explanation: Zooming in makes things look bigger and closer. Zooming out gives you the wider view.
quests.funFact: A ladybug’s bright spots warn birds that it doesn’t taste good.

quests.instruction: Pearl divers swim down to the seabed. When they run short of breath, they quickly…
quests.hint: Divers know where the air is: above them.
quests.explanation: To dive is to go down into the water. To come up is to return toward the surface.
quests.funFact: Some whales can hold their breath for over an hour on a dive.

quests.instruction: The baby is asleep, so the cousins play softly. At the cricket match, the fans cheer…
quests.hint: How do you sound when your team hits a six?
quests.explanation: Softly means making little noise. Loudly means making a lot.
quests.funFact: Very loud sounds can harm your ears, which is why earmuffs are worn at some noisy events.

quests.instruction: Tia stroked the rabbit gently. Squeezing it or pulling its ears would be treating it…
quests.hint: How would the rabbit feel after each kind of touch?
quests.explanation: Gently means with a soft, careful touch. Roughly means with too much force.
quests.funFact: Rabbits have strong back legs, but their bones are surprisingly delicate.

quests.instruction: Imran carried the tray of glasses carefully across the room. His little brother ran with the tray without looking where he was going. He carried it…
quests.hint: Picture each carrier and listen for a crash.
quests.explanation: Carefully means paying attention to avoid mistakes. Carelessly means not paying attention.
quests.funFact: Glass is made mostly from sand that has been heated until it melts.

quests.instruction: After the rain, there were puddles everywhere in the schoolyard. After a whole day of strong sun, you could find them…
quests.hint: Where did the water go?
quests.explanation: Everywhere means in every place. Nowhere means in no place at all.
quests.funFact: Puddles disappear when the water evaporates, turning into invisible vapor in the air.

quests.instruction: Dad tightened the bolts on the swing set. The seat was rubbing against the frame, so he had to…
quests.hint: What do you do to a nut that’s clamped too hard?
quests.explanation: Tightening makes a fastener hold more firmly. Loosening lets it relax a little.
quests.funFact: Spanners come in many sizes so that each one fits a particular nut.

quests.instruction: Hasan missed the best part of the video, so he used the button that goes back. To skip a dull part, he presses…
quests.hint: Think of the button that skips past the dull bit.
quests.explanation: Rewinding takes a video back to an earlier moment. Fast-forwarding moves it ahead.
quests.funFact: Old videotapes had to be wound back and forth by a motor.

quests.instruction: On a cold night, the cat curls up in a tight ball. On a warm day, she…
quests.hint: Which way do you lie when you’re hot?
quests.explanation: Curling up pulls the body in small. Stretching out spreads it long.
quests.funFact: Cats sleep for about twelve to sixteen hours a day.

quests.instruction: Aarav inflated the balloon until it was perfectly round. When the knot slipped, it quickly…
quests.hint: What happens to a balloon when the air rushes out?
quests.explanation: To inflate is to fill with air. To deflate is to let the air out.
quests.funFact: Helium balloons float because helium is lighter than air.

quests.instruction: The hands of a clock move clockwise. Turning a jar lid the other way, to open it, is turning it…
quests.hint: Clock hands have a direction; this answer goes against it.
quests.explanation: Clockwise follows the direction of the clock hands. Anticlockwise goes the opposite way.
quests.funFact: Clock hands move the way sundial shadows move in the northern half of the world.

quests.instruction: In football, the forwards push toward the goal to score. They attack. The players nearest the goal have the job to…
quests.hint: Who tries to stop the ball from going in?
quests.explanation: Attacking means trying to score. Defending means trying to stop the other team from scoring.
quests.funFact: A football team has eleven players on the pitch, including the goalkeeper.

quests.instruction: Dad parked the car in a shady spot. After shopping, he started the engine and…
quests.hint: What does he do once everything is in the boot?
quests.explanation: Parking leaves a vehicle in one place. Driving off takes it away again.
quests.funFact: The first parking meters appeared in Oklahoma City in 1935.

quests.instruction: Rina’s photo was too small to read the sign in it, so she enlarged it. To fit it on a tiny ID card, she had to…
quests.hint: Think about making a picture smaller instead of larger.
quests.explanation: Enlarging makes something bigger. Reducing makes it smaller.
quests.funFact: A magnifying glass makes things look bigger by bending light.

quests.instruction: Maya fell off the monkey bars on her first day. Instead of giving up, she…
quests.hint: What does someone do after a wobbly start if they really want to learn?
quests.explanation: Giving up means stopping because it feels too hard. Keeping on trying means you carry on until you improve.
quests.funFact: Babies fall down many times while learning to walk, and just keep trying.
